note: Small committed summary only; full candidates, docking artifacts, logs and caches remain local (gitignored).
purpose: P3 real-run acceptance test (REVIEW_MINIMAX_ADVICE_20260917 item 4): does loop.progress_signal=safe_vina raise best_safe_composite_global vs the legacy all-candidate vina signal?
conclusions: safe_vina signal drove the safety-gated Vina lower (-8.24 -> -9.03, ~0.8 kcal/mol, directional).
best_safe_composite_global was flat (-0.0007, p=0.93): composite is driven by safety-pass rate, not Vina depth.
safe_run_improvement_rate = 0 in both arms; no run showed sustained safe-Vina improvement.
Safety-gate pass rate fluctuated 0-100% with several rounds at 0: too few safe candidates to demonstrate improvement.
random_gate FAILED (65.8%): random sampling still beats the loop; bottleneck is generator output distribution.
Acceptance NOT met: safe_vina did not raise best_safe_composite_global in this sample.
limitations: n=2 per arm; all Welch p > 0.2; directional evidence only, no statistical power.
Vina and hERG are computational proxies, not measured activity or safety.
Per-run curves use None for rounds with no safety-passing candidate.
Confirmatory runs must pass the random-sampling gate BEFORE statistics are considered meaningful.
